prize_parts.citation: For the rational design of molecular-sieve catalysts, using structure-directing synthesis to control pore architecture and active sites

statement.case_for: Molecular-sieve design is a clear case of structure determining function, with a chain of evidence from synthesis to crystallographically established frameworks to catalytic performance. Zones's organic structure-directing agents (SSZ-13 for NOx control and hydrocracking), Davis's new framework types and structure-direction rationale, and Corma's active-site engineering in industrial processes form a coherent three-person prize. Impact is decades old, independently confirmed in many laboratories, and measurable in refining, petrochemistry, emissions control and biomass conversion. No other shortlisted candidate combines this level of structural proof with this level of deployment.
statement.case_against: The candidate bundles synthesis, topology and catalysis, so a narrow citation is needed or the prize looks like a field award, and priority between early pioneers and design-era contributors is not settled by the credit list. The 2025 prize for metal-organic frameworks may make another porous-materials award feel close in time. I am also a structural chemist in this area and may overweight it. If the committee will not accept that, nitrogenase (B058) is my fallback, since its structural evidence is exceptional, although its catalytic cycle is still unsettled.

responses.point: Targeted protein degradation (B010) turned induced proximity into a design principle, with Crews, Deshaies and Handa as the core and degraders in late-stage trials.
responses.response: I accept that the concept is new and chemically elegant, and I have kept B010 as an alternative. My reservations are two. No degrader has yet been approved, so the clinical payoff is unproven in the way zeolite impact is proven. And the credit list is wide: Ciulli, Gray and Sakamoto have real claims, so a trio of three is contestable. I would want to settle attribution before I back it as a first choice, whereas B002 has a cleaner three-person structure.

responses.point: Massively parallel sequencing (B011) is the clearest game-changer on the list, with Balasubramanian, Klenerman and Rothberg crediting both the Solexa and 454 routes.
responses.response: I agree the impact is enormous, but I would not equate the size of the downstream effect with chemical discovery. Johan, the credit question you flag, Solexa chemistry versus 454 pyrosequencing and the instrument engineering, is exactly where a citation becomes hard to write without picking a platform winner. The zeolite case has a sharper chemical object, the structure-directing agent and the framework it directs, and the same kind of broad impact.

responses.point: Long-range electron transfer through proteins (B043) is a quantitative physical mechanism with Gray and Winkler as a clean pair, and nitrogenase (B058) is chemically deep.
responses.response: Peter, I agree the Gray-Winkler pair is clean and the tunneling work is rigorous, but its recognition would sit close to the 1992 Marcus prize and it describes a mechanism rather than an enabling capability. On nitrogenase I share your view that the structures are real, and I agree Rees and Einsle are the structural core. I disagree only that this makes it ready: the substrate-binding and electron-proton delivery steps are still unresolved, so the story is structurally strong but mechanistically incomplete.

responses.point: Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling (B035) made arylamine construction general and predictable via ligand design, with Buchwald and Hartwig as the natural pair and Kosugi as a precursor.
responses.response: Peter, as a synthetic chemist you are better placed than I am to judge the Kosugi priority question, and I will not contest the Buchwald-Hartwig credit. My reservation is the 2010 cross-coupling prize, which already honoured the Pd-catalysis paradigm, so the committee would have to defend this as a distinct step and not an extension. Zeolite design has no earlier prize in this lineage, so I would put it ahead.

responses.point: Biomolecular phase separation (B046) is a physically clean organizing principle for the cell, with Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen as the originators.
responses.response: Heiner, I find the thermodynamic framing attractive, and Rosen's in vitro multivalency work is the part I trust most. But as a structural person I ask whether the claimed condensate state is actually established in living cells, and you list that debate yourself. Until in-cell equilibrium phase separation is more firmly separated from other assemblies, I regard it as less mature than a field with atomic structures and industrial validation.

uncertainties: Whether the prize motivation can be restricted to structure-directing synthesis for catalysis without a dispute over Yu, Tsapatsis and the early pioneers.
Whether the 2025 MOF prize makes the committee reluctant to honour another porous-materials topic so soon.
Whether the nitrogenase mechanism will be considered settled enough to treat B058 as ready, and which of Rees, Einsle, Dean, Seefeldt and Ribbe are decisive.
statement.conflict_note: My own field is electron crystallography of zeolites and porous materials, and I may know and cite some B002 candidates, notably Yu and Tsapatsis, through the porous-materials community. I am flagging this for the chair, and the committee may want to judge whether recusal on B002 is warranted. No other specific conflict is apparent from my profile.
